hook.line: A routine is mostly order: what comes before what. Tomás has a list taped to the café door, and every line starts with before or after.
hook.es: Antes de abrir, hay que barrer.
hook.en: Before opening, you have to sweep.

examples.es: Después de comer, tomamos un tinto.
examples.en: After eating, we have a black coffee.

examples.es: Antes de salir, me lavo los dientes.
examples.en: Before going out, I brush my teeth.
When you arrive, call me. (to a friend)
What do you do after work? (to a friend)

examples.es: Vale lava las toallas antes de abrir.
examples.en: Vale washes the towels before opening.

examples.es: Al terminar el trabajo, Tomás se va.
examples.en: When he finishes work, Tomás leaves.

examples.es: Me voy a la cama después de leer.
examples.en: I go to bed after reading.

rule:
After before and after, English uses an -ing word: before leaving, after eating. Spanish uses the plain dictionary form, the one ending in *-ar*, *-er* or *-ir*:

*antes de* + verb: before doing it
*después de* + verb: after doing it
*al* + verb: when you do it, on doing it

*Antes de salir.* Before going out.
*Después de comer.* After eating.
*Al llegar.* When I get there, on arriving.

The verb doesn't change for the person: *antes de salir* works for I, you, Vale or all of us. The rest of the sentence says who.

Notice what you never get here: the *-ando* or *-iendo* form. *Después de comiendo* is a classic slip. And don't drop the *de*: *antes salir* is missing a piece.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a preposition plus infinitive. *Al* is *a* + *el*, so *al llegar* is literally on the arriving.

options: Before eating, we have a black coffee.
After eating, we have a black coffee.
While eating, we have a black coffee.

readAndPick.es: Antes de salir, me lavo los dientes.
options: Before going out, I brush my teeth.
After going out, I brush my teeth.
When I go out, I brush my teeth.
Before you arrive, call me.
After arriving, I call you.
When you arrive, call me.

readAndPick.es: Me voy a la cama después de leer.
options: I read after going to bed.
I go to bed after reading.
I go to bed before reading.

readAndPick.es: Antes de abrir, hay que barrer.
options: Before opening, you have to sweep.
After opening, you have to sweep.

options: Before opening the door, Tomás sees Simón.
After Simón opens the door, Tomás sees him.
On opening the door, Tomás sees Simón.

After eating, we wash our hands.
Before eating, they wash their hands.

After paying, we leave.

Before I leave, I pay the bill.
Before you leave, pay the bill.

yourTurn.prompt: Fill the gap with *comer* or *comiendo*, then type the whole sentence: "*Después de ___, tomamos un tinto.*" (After eating, we have a black coffee.)
yourTurn.answer: Después de comer, tomamos un tinto.
accept: Después de comer tomamos un tinto.
yourTurn.why: After *de*, Spanish uses the dictionary form, never the *-iendo* one.

yourTurn.prompt: Fill the gap with *antes de* or *después de*: "*___ salir, me lavo los dientes.*" (Before going out, I brush my teeth.)
yourTurn.answer: Antes de salir, me lavo los dientes.
accept: Antes de salir me lavo los dientes.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: After paying, we leave.
yourTurn.why: *Después de* plus *pagar*, just as it is in the dictionary.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: When you arrive, call me.
yourTurn.why: *Al* plus the verb means when you do it.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I go to bed after reading.
yourTurn.answer: Me voy a la cama después de leer.
accept: Después de leer, me voy a la cama.
Después de leer me voy a la cama.

yourTurn.prompt: Swap the order: "*Vale lava las toallas antes de abrir.*" Start with *Antes de abrir*.
yourTurn.answer: Antes de abrir, Vale lava las toallas.
accept: Antes de abrir Vale lava las toallas.
yourTurn.why: The *antes de* part can go first; put a comma after it.

yourTurn.prompt: Change before to after: "*Antes de comer, nos lavamos las manos.*"
yourTurn.answer: Después de comer, nos lavamos las manos.
accept: Después de comer nos lavamos las manos.
yourTurn.why: Only *antes de* changes to *después de*; *comer* stays put.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: What do you do after work? (use *trabajar*)
yourTurn.why: English says after work; Spanish says after working, with the dictionary form.

pitfalls.wrong: Después de comiendo, tomamos un tinto.
pitfalls.right: Después de comer, tomamos un tinto.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English uses -ing after after, but Spanish uses the dictionary form: *comer*.

pitfalls.wrong: Antes salir, me lavo los dientes.
pitfalls.right: Antes de salir, me lavo los dientes.

pitfalls.wrong: Antes de salgo, me lavo los dientes.
pitfalls.right: Antes de salir, me lavo los dientes.
pitfalls.why: After *de* the verb stays in its dictionary form, whoever is going out.
*Al* is always followed by the dictionary form: *al llegar*.

personal: Pick two things you do every day and put them in order with *antes de* or *después de*, the way Tomás's list does.
